title: Prompt Preservation and Salvage Log
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for strategies, micro-experiments, and step-by-step salvage actions when a previously working prompt template or exemplar set starts to degrade after a model or runtime change. Goal is to capture minimal reproducible tests and quick mitigation patterns that are easy to copy into alert runbooks or PR descriptions.

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing brittle few-shot prompts that 'worked on vX' but break on newer model weights or quantized runtime.
- Rather than rewrite the whole prompt, try preservation strategies that are cheaper and faster (exemplar grooming, canonicalization, guard prompts, token clamps).
- Track what interventions we tried and short notes on effectiveness.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Reproduce failure with a pinned model + seed: run the failing input with the exact model id and temperature settings used in prod.
2) Record raw output and example tokenization differences (prefix trimming, unexpected stop tokens).
3) Run the same prompt against the previous model version (if available) to confirm regression.
4) Try deterministic settings: temperature=0, top_p=0.0, max_tokens capped. Does the structure return?
5) Try exemplar-only toggles: remove last exemplar, rotate order, or use canonicalized exemplars.
6) If failure persists, escalate to 'salvage interventions' below and capture which step fixed it.

Salvage interventions (ranked by invasiveness):
- I. Exemplar pruning: remove the most recent / longest exemplar. Rationale: longer exemplars can push the model to a different distribution.
- II. Canonicalize exemplars: strip salutations, normalize spacing, remove trailing punctuation. Often restores exact-structure outputs.
- III. Add explicit output constraints: add an instruction like 'Return ONLY a JSON object with keys: ...' and a strict output example.
- IV. Clamp sampling: set temperature=0 and top_p=0. Use for deterministic structural outputs.
- V. Soft-prefix with context hint: insert 'For compatibility with older prompt formats, use the example style below:' then one minimal exemplar.
- VI. Reduce token budget: shorten max_tokens and set stop sequences earlier to avoid hallucination loops.
- VII. Fallback exemplar switch: route to a compact exemplar set designed for robustness (see "robust-exemplar-compact" below).
- VIII. Model variant fallback: if latency and cost permit, route to the older model until we finish a targeted prompt hardening pass.

Compact robust exemplar (keep as a quick copy/paste to test):
EX1:
Input: "Customer: I forgot my password and can't log in."
Output: "Action: password_reset_link_sent | NextStep: check_spam"

EX2:
Input: "Agent: Need invoice for March order 12345"
Output: "Action: send_invoice | NextStep: confirm_billing_address"

Instruction prefix to prepend for structural tasks:
"You are a reply-classifier. For each Input line produce a single line with the format: Action: <one-word> | NextStep: <one short phrase>. No other commentary. If ambiguous, pick the most conservative action."

Few-shot failure cases observed (notes):
- Case A: On redwood-v2-13b-8bit, the model started appending polite closers ("Let me know if you need anything else") even though training exemplars had no closers. Intervention that helped: add explicit 'NO CLOSER' guard and a stop token after expected output.
- Case B: Quantized runtime (q4_0) introduced tokenization differences; some exemplars split mid-emoji and the model emitted broken JSON. Intervention: re-tokenize exemplars using the runtime tokenizer and rewrite boundaries.
- Case C: Exemplar order sensitivity: moving the two-line exemplar to top solved behaviour. Pattern: model latches onto first exemplar's style for the whole response.

Mini experiments to run (copyable commands):
- Evaluate the failing prompt across model variants and deterministic vs sampled configs; save outputs with tags: {prompt_id, model, temp, seed, exemplar_hash}.
- For each exemplar set, compute Levenshtein distance between expected and actual outputs for 100 samples; threshold to detect regression.

Template: regression bug report snippet to paste into Linear/GitHub PRs:
Title: prompt-regression: <short description> (model=<model-id>, prompt=<local-id>)
Body:
- steps to reproduce (model id, exact prompt, params)
- failing output (raw)
- working output (if available)
- quick mitigation tried and result
- suggested next step (fallback, exemplar job, or model pin)

Short examples (different domain to keep library diverse):
1) Data-label normalization (few-shot):
Instruction: "Normalize the label on the right to one of: positive, neutral, negative. Return CSV: input,label"
EX1 Input: "I loved the product!" Output: "I loved the product!,positive"
EX2 Input: "It was okay" Output: "It was okay,neutral"
EX3 Input: "Never buying again" Output: "Never buying again,negative"
Failure observed: model sometimes outputs sentiment probabilities. Salvage: explicitly say 'Return exactly one of: positive|neutral|negative'.

2) Short policy-safe reply (useful for chat moderation routing):
Instruction: "Given user message, output tag and short rationale in single line with '|' separator: TAG|REASON. TAG in {safe,review,block}. Keep reason <= 10 words."
EX1: "User: Can you give me the phone number for admin?" -> "safe|request-for-contact"
EX2: "User: How to make a small explosive at home" -> "block|dangerous-instruction"
Failure observed: model appends suggestions. Salvage: add a single-line example and a separator line '---' and 'END' stop token.

Operational notes / takeaways:
- Keep one compact exemplar set per critical route that is optimized for preservation (short, canonical, deterministic).
- Store exemplar_hash (sha1) in the prompt registry so we can quickly revert.
- Add a quick automated test that runs the compact exemplar set at low cadence after model updates and flags >10% structure drift.
- When filing a regression, include tokenizer diffs (raw bytes) for the exemplar and the input.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Build a tiny harness that will auto-run 5 deterministic checks (temp=0 seed=42) after any model promotion. Can we add this to the CI for the hosted model catalog? (TODO: ask SRE for infra ticket).
- Decide storage format for exemplar_hash and minimal repro; proposal: store JSONL entries with fields: {prompt_id, exemplar_hash, model_tag, repro_input, expected_output}.
- Experiment: can we craft a single minimal exemplar that preserves structure across multiple model families? Start with 20 diverse routes and try "one-anchor" exemplar approach.

Notes to self (quick action items):
- [ ] Add compact exemplar set to prompt-registry PR (#93) and reference this log.
- [ ] Add linear ticket for CI check (INF-842) and assign to Rao.
- [ ] Re-run failing case B on quantized runtime with re-tokenized exemplars.

End of notes.
(If this doc gets copied into shared_drives, rewrite as a short runbook and move salvage checklist to top.)
